1. Read the borough dataset (33 rows) into pandas; create a numeric “change” column = first_half_2019_value − second_half_2018_value.  
2. Handling missing data: drop the single borough that has a missing value in either period (list-wise deletion). All computations will then use the remaining 32 boroughs; no other variables contain NAs.  
3. Build the spatial weights matrix W from the supplied neighbor list:  
   • For each borough i, set w_ij = 1 if j is listed as a neighbour of i, else 0.  
   • Symmetrise the matrix (ensure w_ij = w_ji).  
   • Row-standardise W so each row sums to 1 (needed for Moran’s I).  
4. Calculate Global Moran’s I for the “change” vector x:  
      I = (n / Σ_i Σ_j w_ij) * (Σ_i Σ_j w_ij (x_i – ȳ)(x_j – ȳ)) / Σ_i (x_i – ȳ)²  
   where n = 32 and ȳ is the mean change.  
5. Assess significance via a permutation test:  
   • Randomly shuffle the change values across boroughs 10,000 times (≥500 as required).  
   • Recompute Moran’s I for each shuffle to create the null distribution.  
   • p = proportion of permuted I values ≥ observed I (for positive clustering) or ≤ observed I (for negative clustering), using a two-sided test.  
6. Decision rule:  
   • If p < 0.05, conclude that changes are spatially CLUSTERED (report “CLUSTERED”).  
   • Otherwise conclude “NOT CLUSTERED”.  
7. Report: observed Moran’s I and p-value rounded to three decimals in the mandated sentence format.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
data_path = "chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_no2crime_crime_second_half_2018_to_first_half_2019.csv"
adj_path = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(data_path)
adj = pd.read_csv(adj_path)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Compute change and drop rows with any missing values
df["change"] = df["first_half_2019_value"] - df["second_half_2018_value"]
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=["change"]).reset_index(drop=True)

# number of boroughs used
n = len(df_clean)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build symmetric, row-standardised spatial weights matrix W
#    Only keep neighbors that are also in df_clean
boroughs = df_clean["borough"].tolist()
index_map = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}  # borough -> row/col position

# initialise zero matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=float)

# add edges from adjacency list (make symmetric)
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1, b2 = row["borough"], row["neighbor"]
    if b1 in index_map and b2 in index_map:
        i, j = index_map[b1], index_map[b2]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1   # symmetrise

# row-standardise: each row sums to 1  (skip rows with zero degree)
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
    W_standardised = np.divide(W, row_sums, where=row_sums != 0)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Compute observed Global Moran’s I for the change vector
x = df_clean["change"].to_numpy()
x_bar = x.mean()
x_demean = x - x_bar

S0 = W_standardised.sum()          # Σ_i Σ_j w_ij   (after standardisation this is n)
numerator = (x_demean @ W_standardised @ x_demean)
denominator = (x_demean ** 2).sum()
I_obs = (n / S0) * (numerator / denominator)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Permutation test (10,000 permutations) for two-sided p-value
n_perm = 10_000
perm_I = np.empty(n_perm)
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)

for k in range(n_perm):
    x_perm = rng.permutation(x_demean)        # shuffle demeaned values
    perm_I[k] = (n / S0) * ((x_perm @ W_standardised @ x_perm) / denominator)

# two-sided p-value with +1 correction to avoid zero
p_value = (np.sum(np.abs(perm_I) >= np.abs(I_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Verdict
verdict = "CLUSTERED" if (I_obs > 0 and p_value < 0.05) else "NOT CLUSTERED"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Print required outputs
print(f"data_points_used = {n}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (test statistic = {I_obs}, p = {p_value})")
